description:
Sportsbrut , or Corporate Neu-Grunge , Sports Brutalism is a graphic design aesthetic that gained prevalence in the mid-late 2010s, diffusing the high-octane athletic branding with unpolished traits of Neubrutalism , which utilizes aggressive, industrial textures and bold layouts to convey speed, action, and raw kinetic energy.

The aesthetic style leans on a unique middle ground where it is often more maximalist and less glossy than corporate, standard Y2K neu-grunge, but dynamic and slightly more textured than sterile, bold digital neubrutalism.
culturalContext: Key values (per the Aesthetics Wiki): Action, excitement, energy

visualDNA.Overview: The visuals of Sportsbrut are meant to evoke a sense of excitement and energy. Typography tends to be stretched or deformed. Rigid layouts and grids utilize bare-bones box, simple structures that dissect the canvas into harsh and bold chunks. However, key graphic or athlete-themed elements frequently break out of these frame boundaries to shape a sense of forward depth and explosive motion with a high-impact typography where text is compressed, heavily stretched, or distorted along with designers that frequently depend on ultra-condensed, blocky slab fonts or sans-serif to give layouts a imposing, heavy weight.
